questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To experience and explore a place I normally wouldn't have the opportunity to

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Would make more sense to have this question asked earlier in the process since it's been so long since I applied now. I remember most of it to be easy, but there definitely also were some stuff that weren't as clear.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: An orientation week, I guess.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student accommodation and residential colleges

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: No meal plans for the student accommodation but I have a shared kitchen. However, you were obligated to provide/buy all your own kitchen equipments and utensils.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A good thing is that there are a lot of activities you can sign up for, so even if you lived in a studio and have no roommates, it is easy to be social. A not so good thing is that it is very expensive, and there's still stuff you need to buy yourself and you have to pay for six months of rent although you probably won't be here for that long.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Again, can't remember it that well anymore. But there were a specific time frame where you had to enroll and you had to make a prioritized list over the courses you would like to enroll in and which days you would like your tutorials to be.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could e-mail the university questions which I did at one point as I wasn't sure about something with the dates.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I asked for. I was less lucky with the days I wanted but it was possible to change this in the start of the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just to do your research.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Depends on the course/class.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the academic level is higher back home or at least done very differently. There is a lot more focus on theory and it's more academic in Denmark than here. I did do some courses that are quite different to the ones I have at home, so those might have been a bit harder for me to navigate in but not necessarily because I think the level was high - just that it was different from what I am used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Again, less theory. For all of my classes I would have one tutorial and one lecture for each course. The lecture would just be us listening to the lecturer, whereas the tutorials would have less people and most of the times, you would have to work on some small tasks and talk. However, it differed a lot from each tutorial depending on the subject how much engagement you would have to participate in.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Text and Audio Journalism
Visual Communication and Digital Media
Crime and Culture
Popular Culture: From K-Pop to Selfies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I personally especially liked Text and Audio Journalism as it was very practical and the learning style was different in a good way. The assignments were creative and fun as well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Maybe how empty the rooms are and how much you need to buy yourself for the kitchen etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries and housing are really expensive. I pay 1/3 at home for my own 1-bedroom student apartment and here I live with four other people as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of different clubs. Some have to do with where you're from - however, it was mostly clubs for different Asian countries. (none for Northern Europe). Different sports, both basics like football but also bush walking and diving.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you leave in one of the student accommodation, I would definitely recommend to do the free and social activities provided here. You pay a lot of money to live here, so you might as well and it's also a good way to meet people. Sometimes there will also be free food involved, so it might also be a good way to sometimes save a little money.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitely to go and explore other parts of Australia. If you're in Melbourne/Victoria, then do the the great ocean road tour. There are also a lot of nice markets here as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - it's quite similar to our culture at home.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think it's hard to socialize with the locals as you're mostly around other exchange or international students. I personally would've loved to meet more locals, than what I did.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, I think.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness of the Australian people. Also interesting to learn more about Australian history and the indigenous people, especially.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open and participate in the free activities. 
Use your time well, Australia is a very big country so you unfortunately won't be able to experience everything. 
Remember to enjoy yourself and your time here!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Maybe be prepared that a lot of people might be younger than you, especially if you're a bit older yourself when doing the BA. 
I am 25 myself and were living with mainly 18-19 year olds, which sometimes can be a bit tough. They are all very lovely people - however, I find that I am in a different place in my life than most as they for instance have never tried to live by themselves before etc. I was expecting to be older than most, but I didn't expect people here to be that young.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to travel and explore Australia. Also, it's definitely a good life experience to be on your own so far away from everything and everyone you know. I have found myself doing a lot of things that I probably would've been to scared to do normally. You get more adventurous.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Maybe to plan your time here and navigate between travelling, socializing and your studies.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
